2. Facts, in brief, are that the respondent Nos. 1 and 2, as plaintiffs, instituted the above suit for declaration that the order dated 31.12.92 of Additional Divisional Commissioner, Khulna passed in Redemption Appeal No.26 of 1993 allowing redemption of the suit land is illegal and void on the averments that the suit and belonged to defendant No. 1 petitioner who transferred the same to the defendant No.5, the respondent No.6 herein, by kabala dated 28.10.1977 and thus being owner in possession of the suit land the defendant No.5 transferred same to the plaintiff by kabala dated 19.10.87 and also delivered possession of them and thereafter the petitioner created an Ekramama showing that the defendant No.5 executed an agreement on the date of sale to reconvey the said land on receipt of the consideration and on the basis of the same filed an application before the Revenue Court, Bhandaria purportedly under section 95 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act and got an exparte order of redemption dated 9.10.1991 and then having come to know about the above exparte order, the plaintiffs filed an appeal before the Additional Deputy Commissioner (Revenue) Firojpur for setting aside the above order of redemption and after hearing the parties the Additional Deputy Commissioner (Revenue) allowed the appeal holding that the alleged Ekraranama was forged and the order of redemption was thus set aside. Then the petitioner filed an appeal before the Additional Divisional Commissioner, Khulna who by order dated 31.12.1992 allowed the appeal and restored the order of redemption. 

 3. The defendant No. 1/petitioner contested the suit and filed written statement contending that he on 28.10.1977 transferred the suit land to defendant No.5 with condition of reconveyance and on same date the defendant No.5 executed an Ekrarnama in his favour agreeing to recovery the suit land and the basis of said Ekraranama he on, 9.10.1991, got the order of redemption and also got delivery of possession.
